newsitem.title: THAILAND: Burma deports Dutch woman amid student unrest.
newsitem.headline: Burma deports Dutch woman amid student unrest.

text.p: Burma on Monday deported a Dutch woman who it said had been working illegally as a journalist covering student protests in the country.

"She came into the country posing as a tourist but she was actually covering the student incidents. She was found out and deported," a Burmese military government spokesman told Reuters by telephone from Rangoon.
Burma is strict on ensuring journalists have visas.
Recently its embassies abroad have issued journalist visas on a selective basis only ahead of monthly news conferences organised by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).
The deported woman, Williamke Joanna Nyhuis, told Reuters on arrival in Bangkok that she had denied the Burmese charges when interrogated in Rangoon.
She said she was questioned on Sunday by Burmese immigration officials about links with the protesting students and opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi.

"They refused to say why I was being deported but questioned me about whether I had connections with the students, Suu Kyi and other foreigners," she said, adding that she was a regular traveller to Burma.
Nyhuis, 38, declined to disclose her profession.
In the past week, SLORC has faced its biggest challenge from protesting students since troops crushed student-led pro-democracy uprisings in 1988, leaving thousands dead or in jail.
